# MKT·INTEL

> MKT·INTEL is an AI market research agent for any industry. Ask about your own product's market, a competitor or a market trend, and a team of agents searches the live web, reads the best pages in full, verifies every claim with typed decisions and writes a sourced report in minutes.

MKT·INTEL is free to use at https://mkt-intel.vercel.app. A quick brief takes about a minute, and a full playbook report takes two to three minutes. It works for any market with a public web presence: software, consumer brands, retail, fintech, health and more.

## Reports

- Brief: what changed in a market and what to do about it, ranked by impact, with a confidence and impact score for each finding.
- Competitor profile: side-by-side profiles of each competitor (positioning, pricing, customers, strengths and weaknesses) plus a positioning map.
- Pricing teardown: every tier and hidden cost, what a typical customer pays on each, and how clear each pricing page is for human buyers and AI agents.
- Battlecard: where each side wins, answers to common objections, questions that expose weak spots, and who should pick which.
- Market landscape: a market map of every player by category and stage, a capability matrix, SWOT for a new entrant, trends and emerging players.
- Customer pain: complaints ranked by share of mentions, with real quotes from reviews and forums, feature requests, affected segments and unmet gaps.
- Market sizing: TAM, SAM and SOM built from sourced inputs. The app multiplies the inputs itself and flags any figure that does not match. Also growth history, forecasts and bear, base and bull cases.
- Opportunity: segments scored by demand and competition, market gaps, risks with likelihood and impact, and a go, conditional or no-go call with first steps.

Every report includes charts, a methodology section (sources read, verified findings, research completeness per topic, named gaps, contradictions) and a source-quality score for each source.

## Downloads

Every report downloads as a designed PDF, a PowerPoint deck with native, editable charts, an Excel workbook (one sheet per table, with source links), Markdown or JSON.

## How it works

- Plan: works out which companies, sources and official pages to check.
- Research: searches the live web (Context.dev, with Tavily and Firecrawl as fallbacks) and reads the best pages in full.
- Verify: extracts every claim with its source and flags where sources disagree.
- Decide: Jev typed decisions (or a built-in decision agent) score whether each finding is real, what kind it is and how big the impact is. Weak evidence triggers another round of research.
- Write: produces the report. Unverified claims are labelled, never stated as fact.

## Example questions

- What are the biggest trends in home fitness right now?
- Pricing teardown of Shopify vs BigCommerce
- Competitor profile of Notion, Coda and Confluence
- HubSpot vs Salesforce for a 50-person sales team
- How is Oatly positioned against its competitors?
